/-- The least positive integer `n` such that `77` divides `(n + 2) * (n + 3)`.
Must be a numeric literal. -/

/-- `p07_answer` is the least element of the set of positive `n` with
`77 ∣ (n + 2) * (n + 3)`. -/
theorem p07_least_divisible :
    IsLeast {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ 77 ∣ (n + 2) * (n + 3)} p07_answer := by
  -- First we show that `19` belongs to the set.
  have hdiv : 77 ∣ (p07_answer + 2) * (p07_answer + 3) := by
    -- `(19+2)*(19+3) = 21*22 = 77*6`
    exact ⟨6, by norm_num⟩
  have hmem : p07_answer ∈ {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ 77 ∣ (n + 2) * (n + 3)} := by
    exact ⟨by decide, hdiv⟩
  refine ⟨hmem, ?_⟩
  -- Now we prove minimality: any other element of the set is at least `19`.
  intro m hm
  -- Suppose, for a contradiction, that `m < 19`.  Then we would obtain a
  -- counterexample to the fact that no number `< 19` satisfies the property.
  have hnot : ¬ 19 > m := by
    intro hgt
    have hlt : m < 19 := hgt
    have h_ex : ∃ n, n < 19 ∧ 0 < n ∧ 77 ∣ (n + 2) * (n + 3) :=

    have hfalse : ¬ ∃ n, n < 19 ∧ 0 < n ∧ 77 ∣ (n + 2) * (n + 3) := by
      decide
    exact hfalse h_ex
  exact Nat.le_of_not_gt hnot
